prose.summary: The aluminium window frames meet the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. This results in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED. See the checklist below for the steps to claim the preference.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and a value addition (VA) of at least 45%. CTSH means each non‑originating input must be classified in a different 6‑digit subheading than the product, while VA is the share of the product's price that does not come from non‑originating materials, calculated on an FOB basis. The final manufacture took place in the UAE, the work goes beyond the minimal operations, all three non‑originating inputs satisfy the tariff shift, and the value addition of 49.0% exceeds the 45% threshold.

notes.text: If the producer is located in a free zone, it is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India. The 40% value‑added letter is a Factory Registration condition only and is not the CEPA product‑specific rule test.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The final manufacture and the operations described are the exporter's own declaration.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate shown.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022), not the official text.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India.
The 40% value-added letter is a Factory Registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
